entries.description: path to LoRA adapter (use comma-separated values to load multiple adapters)
entries.notes: Comma-separated adapter paths load at scale 1.0 in listed order and fuse into the base weights at model load (#1439); fusion adds deltas, so multi-adapter results are order-independent while logs and failure attribution stay deterministic. The mlxcel-native --adapter spelling remains an alias. Runtime swappability is the POST /lora-adapters entry's business.

entries.description: load LoRA adapters without applying them (apply later via POST /lora-adapters) (default: disabled)
entries.notes: Accepted on both binaries: adapters are validated at load (a broken adapter still fails startup) and GET /lora-adapters reports them at scale 0.0, upstream's initial state. Deferred because the flag's purpose, applying the adapters later through POST /lora-adapters, needs runtime (unfused) LoRA application that mlxcel does not have (#1439).
divergence: The loaded-but-unapplied adapters can never be applied afterwards: POST /lora-adapters refuses the scale change where b10621 activates them at runtime (#1439).

entries.description: path to LoRA adapter with user defined scaling (format: FNAME:SCALE,...) note: use comma-separated values
entries.notes: Comma-separated FNAME:SCALE pairs (split on the last colon so absolute paths keep their separators) fuse with the user scale multiplied into the adapter's own alpha/r, exactly as upstream multiplies its per-adapter scale. A non-numeric, NaN, or infinite scale fails startup: fusing a non-finite delta would poison every weight the adapter touches (#1439).

Reports every configured adapter in b10621's entry shape: id, path, scale (0.0 for a loaded-but-not-applied adapter, upstream's --lora-init-without-apply report), task_name and prompt_prefix (empty: b10621 reads them from GGUF adapter metadata, which MLX adapter directories do not carry; upstream reports empty strings for adapters without that metadata too). The alora invocation keys appear only for alora adapters upstream, and no MLX adapter is one.

Mounted with upstream's request contract: a non-array body answers the exact "Request body must be an array" 400, entries are resolved with upstream's construct_lora_list rule (listed ids set their scale, unlisted drop to 0.0, unknown ids are ignored), and a request resolving to the configuration already in force answers {"success": true}.
divergence: A request that changes any adapter scale is refused with a diagnostic naming --lora-scaled and a restart; b10621 applies the new scales at runtime. mlxcel fuses adapters into the weights at load, so a runtime swap requires the unfused-LoRA forward path this entry stays deferred for (#1439).

entries.description: A list of LoRA adapters to apply to this request. Each entry must have `id` and `scale` fields. Adapters not listed default to scale 0.0
entries.notes: Declared on NativeCompletionRequest and resolved with upstream's rule (listed ids set scales, unlisted drop to 0.0). A value resolving to the fused configuration is accepted as inert, which is also what it means upstream; a different per-request adapter set is refused with a 400 naming GET /lora-adapters and --lora-scaled, following the #1441 policy of refusing rather than silently serving on weights the client did not ask for.
divergence: Per-request adapter selection cannot change the served weights: any non-inert value is refused where b10621 swaps the slot's adapter set for that request (#1439).
